silo_relevance: This paper is relevant to portfolio_optimization because it evaluates models directly through long-short portfolio construction and out-of-sample Sharpe ratio, which are core portfolio selection objectives. Its main value for this silo is showing that a hybrid quantum-temporal model can improve ranking-based stock selection and portfolio performance under noisy, regime-shifting market conditions.

key_points.point: The evaluation is portfolio-native: predictions are turned into long-short portfolios and scored by out-of-sample annualized Sharpe ratio.
key_points.silo_note: This directly matches portfolio optimization objectives, where the key question is whether signals improve risk-adjusted portfolio returns rather than standalone prediction accuracy.

key_points.point: QTCNN delivers the strongest reported portfolio performance, with the highest out-of-sample Sharpe ratio among tested models.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio optimization, the main takeaway is that the model improves the quality of asset ranking/selection enough to translate into better portfolio-level risk-adjusted returns.

key_points.point: The setup uses a liquid-stock universe and cross-sectional daily normalization, which are important preprocessing choices for tradable portfolio construction.
key_points.silo_note: These choices matter because portfolio optimization depends on investable assets and stable cross-sectional signals, not just raw predictive features.

key_points.point: The weakly supervised top-vs-bottom labeling scheme aligns with ranking assets for long-short allocation.
key_points.silo_note: This is especially relevant to portfolio optimization because it trains the model to separate winners from losers, which is the same structure used when forming long-short portfolios.

key_points.point: Ablation results show that the quantum circuit and entanglement add incremental Sharpe improvement over a classical temporal model.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio optimization, this suggests the quantum component may improve the portfolio signal beyond what a classical sequence model can provide, which is what matters for allocation decisions.
